Uldum (/ˌuːlˈduːm/ OOL-DOOM) is an ancient desert located on the southern coast of Kalimdor, surrounded by the Un'Goro Crater in the north, Tanaris in the east and Silithus in the northwest. It is the homeland of stone-cat people known as tol'vir and is rich with titan lore.
A superweapon is rumored to exist in Uldum which the Alliance, Horde and Deathwing's minions seek. There is no super weapon, however; Uldum is the weapon, intended to wipe out all life on Azeroth in case Algalon the Observer's Reply-Code Omega went through to the titans.

For years historians have explored southern Kalimdor for a means of entry into this ancient titan land, searching for more evidence of Azeroth's origins. But the [[Cataclysm (event)|Cataclysm]] will change everything, for the facade behind which Uldum has been tucked for millennia will be ruptured, leaving powerful mysteries vulnerable to discovery by the bravest, smartest, or perhaps even most brutal explorers.|Cataclysm features: Halls of Origination[http://web.archive.org/web/20120107042802/http://www.worldofwarcraft.com/cataclysm/features/origination.html Archived page]}} '''Uldum''' ({{IPA|/ˌuːlˈduːm/}} {{respell|OOL-DOOM}}) is an ancient desert located on the southern coast of [[Kalimdor]], surrounded by the [[Un'Goro Crater]] in the north, [[Tanaris]] in the east and [[Silithus]] in the northwest. It is the homeland of stone-cat people known as [[tol'vir]] and is rich with [[titan]] lore. A superweapon is rumored to exist in Uldum which the Alliance, Horde and Deathwing's minions seek. There is no super weapon, however; Uldum ''is'' the weapon, intended to wipe out all life on Azeroth in case [[Algalon the Observer]]'s [[Reply-Code Omega]] went through to the [[titan]]s.{{ref web|url=http://g4tv.com/videos/50255/Uldum-Guide---WoW-Cataclysm/|title=Uldum Guide - WoW: Cataclysm|date=2010-12-08|accessdate=2010-12-31|publisher=G4tv.com}} ==History== [[File:Chronicle Uldum.jpg|thumb|The [[titan-forged]] stronghold of Uldum, the [[Halls of Origination]].]] The region of Uldum was once a vast jungle, dotted with pristine lakes and waterfalls.{{Ref WoWCV1|85|87}} During the ordering of [[Azeroth]], [[Ra|Highkeeper Ra]] and his followers — the [[anubisath]]s, the [[tol'vir]] and the [[mogu]] — installed the [[Forge of Origination]] in Uldum. The Forge would regulate the rhythms of the earth and fortify the [[worldsoul]]'s form, but would also be able to completely reoriginate the planet in case of systemic corruption. After installing the Forge, Ra assigned some of the tol'vir and anubisaths to watch over the region, while he and the rest of his followers continued west to establish the prison of [[Ahn'Qiraj]] to house the defeated [[Old God]] [[C'Thun]].{{Ref WoWCV1|36|37}} Around 15,000-12,200 [[BDP]], Ra was imprisoned by [[Lei Shen]], the Thunder King, who used the Highkeeper's powers to become the first emperor of the [[mogu empire]]. Learning from Ra of the demise of the [[Pantheon of Order]], Lei Shen declared that he would carry on the work of the [[titan]]s and led an army of his mogu warriors and [[Zandalari Empire|Zandalari]] allies into Uldum, seeking to claim the Forge of Origination — believing it to hold the secrets of eternal life. The tol'vir knew they could not defeat the Thunder King and his armies in battle, and so instead turned to another tactic. While some of the tol'vir remained outside the fortress to hold off the invading armies, the ones inside activated the Forge. They knew that using the weapon to its full potential would wipe out all life on the planet, and so instead had configured it to only scour the nearby land. Waves of energy erupted from the Forge, bathing the surrounding lands in the powers of uncreation and instantly killing Lei Shen and his entire army; however, it also devastated the surrounding lands, turning Uldum into a barren desert. The surviving tol'vir then worked to ensure that no one would ever attempt to claim Uldum again, and shrouded the mountain passes leading into the region with magic, sealing the land off from the eyes of mortals. The dead Zandalari who had followed [[Zulathra]] were buried at [[Kings' Rest]] in the [[Halls of Ash]].[[Kings' Rest#Halls of Ash]] Long ago, the [[tol'vir]] weaponsmith [[Irmaat]] was known all throughout Uldum for his excellent work in creating magical weapons that represent the [[Air elemental|air spirits]] that live there.[[The Legend of the Sands]] The city of [[Ruins of Ahmtul|Ahmtul]] was destroyed by raw elemental fury when Irmaat tried to bind the power of [[Al'Akir|Al'Akir the Windlord]] within a [[Fists of the Heavens|set of fist weapons]]. ===Cataclysm=== {{Cata-section}} Following the [[Cataclysm (event)|Cataclysm]] in 28 [[ADP]], the elemental unrest had destroyed the enchanted barrier, allowing [[Al'Akir]] and his [[air elemental]]s to emerge from their domain in the [[Elemental Plane]], the [[Skywall]], through a rift in the ancient land of Uldum. On the orders of [[Deathwing]], Al'Akir sought to harness the ability of the [[Forge of Origination]], the power to scour every creature from [[Azeroth]]. At the request of the [[Earthen Ring]], the [[Alliance]] and [[Horde]] [[adventurer]]s secured the ancient forge before the [[Twilight's Hammer]] could harness its energies, but also delivered a crushing blow to the [[Old God]] [[N'Zoth]]'s elemental minions by vanquishing the Windlord himself within his own domain.{{Ref WoWCV3|205}} ===Legion=== {{Legion-section}} After the death of [[Al'Akir]], the [[djinn]] [[Typhinius]] recovered the Fists of the Heavens and took control of the air elementals. When the [[Burning Legion]] invaded in 32 ADP, Typhinus commanded his air minions to raid Uldum, the Fists of the Heavens sweeping away all early resistance. However, as it turned out, the air elementals still did not recover from their prior civil war and were weakened, and Typhinus had not properly mastered them. Soon, the attack on Uldum ended.[[The Chronicle of Ages#Fists of the Heavens]] ===Battle for Azeroth=== {{bfa-section}} When [[Sargeras]] struck [[Azeroth]] with his sword, he unearthed new tombs, and from one the [[Amathet]] emerged. They speak little to other tol'vir, believing them to be betrayers of their sacred duties. They believe that they, stewards of the [[titan]]s, should alone control the [[:Azerite]]. When they realized that [[Rajh]] and his kin were slain, they constructed their own [[Uldum watcher|new keepers]], which means they must have an active forge like the [[Forge of Wills]] and [[Forge of Origination]].[[Glittering Scarab (quest)]] In Year 33 ADP, the Amathet tol'vir began to assault the Halls of Origination and surrounding areas of Uldum, bringing them in conflict with the Ramkahen. The Ramkahen formed the [[Uldum Accord]] by allying with the [[Explorers' League]] and [[Wastewander]] bandits. They defended Uldum and the Halls of Origination from both [[N'Zoth]]'s forces and the Amathet.[[The Uldum Accord]] ==Geography== [[File:Ramkahen by Nightfall.jpg|thumb|The city of [[Ramkahen]] and the surrounding areas.]] Uldum is a research facility for the titans in their continuing efforts to enhance the biosphere of Azeroth. Specific information regarding their work as it relates to Uldum is unknown and can only be accessed with the [[Plates of Uldum]].[[Stone Watcher of Norgannon]] [[Prospector Gunstan]] maintained a lonely vigil near the outside gates on behalf of the [[Explorers' League]]. Since then, he has been joined by a number of his fellow explorers, with the rival blood elven [[Reliquary]] setting up camp nearby. The landscape of Uldum is predominately desert, with a large river surrounded by an oasis flowing through the center of the region, mostly populated by the [[tol'vir]], with the largest settlement - the [[Lost City of Tol'vir|Lost City]] located on the river delta. The western part of Uldum consists of a large expanse of the wind-swept dunes with half-buried Tol'vir settlements and pyramids, caused by the recent transgressions of [[Al'Akir]]'s air elemental minions. In the east lies a massive pyramid that houses the [[titan]] complex known as the [[Halls of Origination]]. The northwestern part is the location of the [[Obelisk of the Stars]] and [[Gate of Unending Cycles|The Gate of Unending Cycles]] connecting the region with [[Tanaris]] desert. The southern part of the region besides the river delta is mostly cliffs, with settlements held by the [[Neferset]]. The southwestern part is being held by an expedition led by [[Commander Schnottz]]. The Cataclysm also brought the [[Skywall]] towers into Uldum that serve as an entrance to the Al'Akir's domain - the [[elemental plane]] of air. Al'Akir sends his elemental minions to convince the Tol'vir to join his new liege [[Deathwing]], even rewarding them with removal of the [[Curse of Flesh]]. Those who dared to oppose suffered dire consequences as exampled in the [[Orsis]] settlement. The animals that live there are [[scorpid]]s, [[hyena]]s, [[camel]]s, and more. '''{{Neutral}} [[Flight path]]s from [[Schnottz's Landing]]''' *{{Neutral}} [[Oasis of Vir'sar]], Uldum *{{Neutral}} [[Ramkahen]], Uldum ===Adjacent regions=== {| class="darktable" |- !Zone Name !Faction !Level Range !Direction !Access |- |[[Tanaris]] || {{Alliance}}{{Horde}} || 40 - 60 |Northeast || By foot or by flying |- |[[Un'Goro Crater]] || {{Alliance}}{{Horde}} || 40 - 60 |North || By flying |- |[[Silithus]] || {{Alliance}}{{Horde}} || 40 - 60 |Northwest || By flying |- |[[Ahn'Qiraj: The Fallen Kingdom]] || {{Alliance}}{{Horde}} || N/A |West || By flying |} ===Portals=== There are portals to Uldum from the earthshrines in [[Stormwind]] and [[Orgrimmar]]. They unlock after players wind up in [[Ramkahen]] after completing the [[Uldum quests#Escape and retribution|first few mandatory quests]] starting with [[Easy Money]] from [[Adarrah]] in [[Tanaris]]. There are no portals from Uldum back to Stormwind/Orgrimmar, however. ==Notable characters== {{Seealso|Uldum NPCs}} [[File:Cata-UldumDamNight.jpg|thumb|The [[Vir'naal Dam]] at night.]] *{{RaceIcon|Human|Female}} {{NPC|Neutral|Adarrah}} *{{RaceIcon|BloodElf|Male}} {{NPC|Horde|Belloc Brightblade}} *{{RaceIcon|Brann}} {{NPC|Alliance|Brann Bronzebeard}} *{{RaceIcon|Human|Male}} {{NPC|Neutral|Budd Nedreck}} *{{RaceIcon|Goblin|Male}} {{NPC|Neutral|Commander Schnottz}} *{{RaceIcon|Human|Male}} {{NPC|Alliance|Harrison Jones}} *{{RaceIcon|Ramkahen}} {{NPC|Neutral|Prince Nadun}} *{{RaceIcon|Ramkahen}} {{NPC|Neutral|King Phaoris}} *{{RaceIcon|Djinni}} {{NPC|Combat|Siamat}} ==Quests== {{Main|Uldum quests}} ==Resources== '''Herbalism''' *[[Cinderbloom]] *[[Whiptail (herb)]] '''Mining''' *[[Elementium Ore]] *[[Pyrite Ore]] ==Wild creatures== {{Columns|2| *[[Armadillo]]s *[[Camel]]s *[[Carrion bird]]s **[[Vulture]]s *[[Coyote]]s *[[Fox]]es *[[Gazelle]]s *[[Hyena]]s *[[Lion]]s *[[Crocolisk]]s *[[Scarab]]s *[[Scorpid]]s *[[Sea serpent]]s *[[Snake]]s *[[Tiger]]s *[[Wasp]]s }} ==Mysteries in the Sands== {{Book|Uldum |height=29em|align=left|content=I'm not a prophet; I'm just a gnome who trusts her gut. After the first small tremors started shaking Azeroth, my instincts told me that something even bigger was on its way. Unfortunately, no one else in [[Gadgetzan]] shared my healthy paranoia of the coming apocalypse. The old codgers in the just snickered behind my back when I decided to live in the skies over [[Tanaris]] aboard my trusty frying machine, only coming down for food and fuel when absolutely necessary. When the "big one" finally hit as I'd predicted, they weren't laughing anymore. As the dunes around Gadgetzan rose and fell in the waves, all those skeptics were crying like babies while I was safe and sound high in the sky. But I didn't expect what happened next: just over the mountains in southern Tanaris, land appeared out of thin air. Not ''just'' land, but some kind of civilization with towering obelisks and pyramids covered in strange symbols. A thought ran through my head that this might be the legendary region of Uldum. I wrote the idea off as harebrained until dozen of would-be adventurers started showing up in Gadgetzan, whispering Uldum's name and babbling on about treasure hoards hidden with the area. With all these fresh faces around, I've been making a fortune selling aerial tours over the mountains near Uldum. More importantly, those disbelievers who treated me like a nut before the quake hit have begun show me the respect I deserve. If they keep it up, I might just offer them one of my tours...maybe even at a discount! -[[Kleesa Gearspring]] of Gadgetzan.''[[The Art of Cataclysm]]'', pg. 126}} ==In the RPG== {{RPG-section}} It is said that [[Tanaris]] once housed a [[Titan]] [[city]], a place known as '''Uldum'''. The city seems to be lost as no one has been able to find it. Perhaps the sands cover it, or maybe Uldum is just another name for the [[Caverns of Time]].''[[Lands of Mystery]]'', pg. 59 [[Gadgetzan]], a goblin trading post in Tanaris, is where many [[Ironforge (kingdom)|Ironforge]] [[prospector]]s stock up on supplies before heading out in search of the lost Titan city of Uldum.''[[World of Warcraft: The Roleplaying Game]]'', pg. 19 Fragments of notes unearthed from [[Bael Modan]] suggest that a great titan city lies deep within the rocky expanse of the southern desert. So far, [[Dwarf|dwarven]] expeditions have yet to track down the location of Uldum, but they are confident that it is only a matter of time.''[[Warcraft: The Roleplaying Game]]'', pg. 211 ==Notes and trivia== *The [[earthen]] and the [[stone trogg]]s somehow found their way to [[Deepholm]] through Uldum more than fifteen thousand years ago.[[To Stonehearth's Aid]] *When ''Cataclysm'' was released, there was a minor bug in this zone that caused players to pop in and out of combat randomly. It only really was an inconvenience when you wanted to mount, and was eventually fixed. *In the early concept map, the [[Twilight's Hammer]] cult had three camps in the zone.
